<!-- generated by FlowCast Studio from https://wso2.com/integration-platform/docs/connectors/catalog/messaging/asb/example -->

## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `Examples`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `asb-example`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **Examples**.

## Step 2: Search for the ASB connector in the palette

1. Select **Add Connection** in the WSO2 Integrator panel to open the connector search palette, then search for **Azure Service Bus**.

## Step 3: Fill in the connection parameters

1. Select **Azure Service Bus** connector card to open the configuration form.
2. <!-- manual: Bind each field to a configurable variable: - config : The ASBServiceSenderConfig record expression containing entityType, topicOrQueueName, and connectionString, each bound to a configurable variable - connectionName : The name used to identify this connection on the canvas -->

## Step 4: Save the connection

1. Select **Save Connection** to persist the connection.

## Step 5: Set actual values for your configurables

1. In the left panel, select **Configurations**.
2. Run the shell command `.venv/bin/python tools/write_config.py --project asb-example --expect asbConnectionString,asbEntityPath,asbQueueName` to set the configurable values.

## Step 6: Add an Automation entry point

1. <!-- manual: Navigate to the MessageSenderAutomation integration overview. -->
2. Select **Add Artifact**.
3. Under **Automation**, select **Automation** tile.
4. Select **Create** to confirm with default settings.

## Step 7: Select and configure the Send operation

1. On the canvas, select **⊕** node between **Start** and **Error Handler**.
2. Select **asbMessagesender** under **Connections**.
3. Select **Send** to open the configuration form.
4. <!-- manual: In the Expression tab, enter an asb:Message record with body, contentType, and label values. -->
5. Select **Save**.
6. Wait 8 seconds.

## Step 8: Open the Add connection panel

1. In the WSO2 Integrator side panel, hover over **Connections** and select **+**.
2. <!-- manual: hover over Connections -->
3. <!-- manual: In the search field, enter asb to filter connectors. -->
4. Select **ASB MessageReceiver** from the results.

## Step 9: Fill in the connection parameters

1. <!-- manual: Bind each connection parameter to a configurable variable so sensitive values are supplied at runtime. - connectionString : The Azure Service Bus primary or secondary connection string - entityConfig : A QueueConfig record specifying the target queue name (asbQueueName) - Connection Name : A unique name for this connection; enter asbMessagereceiver -->

## Step 10: Save the connection

1. Select **Save** to persist the connection.

## Step 11: Set actual values for your configurables

1. In the left panel, select **Configurations**.
2. Run the shell command `.venv/bin/python tools/write_config.py --project asb-example --expect asbConnectionString,asbEntityPath,asbQueueName` to set the configurable values.

## Step 12: Add an Automation entry point

1. In the WSO2 Integrator side panel, hover over **Entry Points** and select **+**.
2. <!-- manual: hover over Entry Points -->
3. Select **Automation** from the artifacts panel.
4. Leave the default name (`main`) and select **Create**.

## Step 13: Select and configure the Receive operation

1. Select **+** button on the placeholder between **Start** and **Error Handler** to open the step panel.
2. Select **asbMessagereceiver** under **Connections**.
3. Select **Receive** to open the operation configuration panel.

## Step 14: Open the Artifacts palette

1. Select **+ Add Artifact** in the WSO2 Integrator canvas to open the Artifacts palette.
2. Select **Event Integration**.

## Step 15: Bind listener parameters to configurable variables

1. <!-- manual: Select inside the Connection String field, then select the Open Helper Panel icon to open the helper panel. -->
2. Go to the **Configurables** tab and select **+ New Configurable**.
3. Set **Variable Name** to `connectionString`.
4. Set **Variable Type** to `string`, then select **Save**. The `connectionString` tag appears in the field.
5. Select **+ New Configurable** again, set **Variable Name** to `queueName` and **Variable Type** to `string`, then select **Save**.
6. In the **Entity Config** field, select **Expression** toggle.
7. Search for `{ queueName: queueName }`.
8. Confirm that **Listener Name** is set to `asbListener`.

## Step 16: Set actual values for your configurations

1. Select **Configurations** in the left panel of WSO2 Integrator to open the Configurations panel, then set a value for each configuration listed below: - **connectionString** (string) : The full Azure Service Bus namespace connection string, for example `Endpoint=sb://‹NAMESPACE›.servicebus.windows.net/;SharedAccessKeyName=‹KEY_NAME›;SharedAccessKey=‹KEY_VALUE›` - **queueName** (string) : The name of the queue to consume messages from, for example `my-queue`
2. <!-- manual: Select Configurations in the left panel of WSO2 Integrator to open the Configurations panel, then set a value for each configuration listed below: - connectionString (string) : The full Azure Service Bus namespace connection string, for example Endpoint=sb://‹NAMESPACE›.servicebus.windows.net/;SharedAccessKeyName=‹KEY_NAME›;SharedAccessKey=‹KEY_VALUE› - queueName (string) : The name of the queue to consume messages from, for example my-queue -->

## Step 17: Create the trigger

1. Select **Create** to submit the form and generate the service scaffold.

## Step 18: Add the onMessage handler

1. In the service view, select **+ Add Handler**.

## Step 19: Inspect the initial handler flow canvas

1. Select **onMessage** from the side panel to register the handler. > **Note:** Azure Service Bus uses the library-defined `asb:Message` type; there's no **Define Value / Create Type Schema** modal for this trigger.
2. Select **onMessage** row in the service view to open the flow canvas.

## Step 20: Add the log:printInfo step

1. Select **+** icon in the flow chart.
2. In the side panel that opens, select **Log Info** from the **Logging** section.
3. <!-- manual: enter message.toJsonString() as the message -->

## Step 21: Return to the service view

1. Select the back arrow or select **Azure Service Bus Event Integration** in the breadcrumb to return to the service view and confirm the `onMessage` handler row is registered under **Event Handlers**.
